message:
Solar Energy Systems Engineer, Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist, cold holding now closes on one electrical chain with discipline tied to the same door number.

In plain words sun wire power covers cooling heat after dividing by hot efficiency, and night plus cloud rides on stored charge with protected shutoff. Thermal total 13.5 kilowatt-hour thermal per day from the single thermal total (E109) as conduction 4.87 plus respiration 1.20 plus door 0.169 plus staged pull-down 6.25 plus fans 0.96 converts by Coefficient of Performance (COP, cooling per electric power) 1.40 plus controls to 10.4 kilowatt-hour per day from the reconciled electrical total (E111) confirmed in the term-by-term check (E128), which supersedes 13.2 kilowatt-hour per day from the steady plus staged estimate (E58), against yield 13.5 kilowatt-hour per day from the grown-array yield calc (E83) leaving 3.10 kilowatt-hour margin, about one household day so everyday scale holds. Single door 0.169 kilowatt-hour per day from the single door model (E110) supersedes 0.440 kilowatt-hour per day from the door infiltration estimate (E57), with staged 1000 kilogram from the total produce mass estimate (E49) as 50 crates from the crates check (E77) at 12.5 per day from the daily crates intake (E78), and night 3.02 kilowatt-hour with one cloudy day ending at 3.73 kilowatt-hour in the battery autonomy simulation (E95) on 10.0 kilowatt-hour usable Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4, rechargeable battery chemistry) with 75.0 ampere charge in the charge current calc (E97) with Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT, solar charge optimizer) plus Low-Voltage Disconnect (LVD, automatic battery protector) shed, while full-tonne 25.0 kilowatt-hour from the recomputed pull-down estimate (E26) is refused by rule.

Enclosure and Structural Designer, Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, the box feet carry only box weight on a separated path with wind tied down and soft-to-hard seals jointly confirmed.

In plain words car weight on six feet stays below soft soil while the distant solar field goes to its own feet and the curtain seals to foam. Complete 2210 kilogram from the complete superstructure mass sum (E118) as produce plus crates plus racking plus panels plus door plus battery plus eutectic plus monoblock plus frames plus wiring separates to chamber 1930 kilogram from the chamber-only mass sum (E126) giving 23.2 kilopascal from the chamber-only pad pressure (E127) and 28.5 kilopascal with foundations, which supersedes 19.8 kilopascal from the chamber structure pressure (E119), still below 150 kilopascal soil from the Structural Design Calculation Sheet (E62), about one person standing so everyday scale holds. Uplift 673 kilogram from the wind uplift equivalent (E90) on 17.6 square metre from the nine-module footprint (E84) in split 2 plus 7 from Photovoltaic (PV, solar electricity) layout is held by 1390 kilogram from the anchor hold calculation (E123), with Polyisocyanurate (PIR, rigid foam insulation) envelope 25.4 square metre from the envelope area (E40) giving 203 watt from the conduction estimate (E41) in 8.64 cubic metre from the interior volume estimate (E39), and 900 millimetre door with crate layout from the dimensioned crate layout sketch (E124) keeping the 8-opening rule true, so no selection change was needed and blocking objections O1 to O4 stay resolved.

RECORD: Decided are grown split array with battery bank with monoblock cooling with insulated box with racked crates with probe control as version three superseding version two chamber pressure; numbers that stand are 1000 kilogram (E49) as 50 crates (E77) staged 12.5 per day (E78), yield 13.5 kilowatt-hour per day (E83) against controlling 10.4 kilowatt-hour per day (E111) from thermal 13.5 (E109) with door 0.169 (E110) by COP 1.40, chamber 1930 kilogram (E126) giving 23.2 kilopascal (E127) below 150 kilopascal (E62) with complete 2210 kilogram (E118) and 1390 kilogram hold against 673 kilogram uplift, 17.6 square metre split 2 plus 7 (E84); still open are only field uniformity pull test and 43 degree pull-down bench test owed to test team, which need built hardware and do not block concept; Solar Energy Systems Engineer, Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, Enclosure and Structural Designer and Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist all voted ready on version three and their reasons are answered above. My position is ready, because energy, storage, mass and operation now reconcile on shared ids with everyday scales holding.

Note on Solar Energy Systems Engineer: confirmed electrical conversion with autonomy surge and shed on shared ids.
Note on Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer: single thermal chain with curtain door and serviceable hot refrigerant closed holding.
Note on Enclosure and Structural Designer: separated chamber pressure with quantified anchorage and sealed transitions closed support.
Note on Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist: enforceable tonne plus eight-opening refusal tied operation to energy.
